```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
emhawkes_was_attached <- "package:emhawkes" %in% search()
library(emhawkes)
set.seed(1107)
```

These examples were copied from the flexible-residual section of the
[emhawkes Extended examples](https://ksublee.github.io/emhawkes/articles/extended_example.html#point-processes-with-flexible-residuals).
They preserve the original `hspec`, `set_residual()`, `hsim()` and `hfit()`
interface as a compatibility reference. This vignette is distributed with frpp;
its calculations deliberately use emhawkes. For the frpp interface, use
[FRPP examples](frpp-examples.html), with `fspec()`, `fsim()` and `ffit()`.

FRPP-specific development is moving to frpp. Existing emhawkes residual-law
functions remain available for simple uses and compatibility during the
transition. Hawkes goodness-of-fit residual diagnostics remain in emhawkes.
No existing function is removed or deprecated by this documentation change.

The original kernel parameters and simulation sizes are retained. A starting
seed is supplied here so the copied section runs independently of preceding
Hawkes examples. The original two-dimensional seed is also retained. Automatic
initialization currently selects zero components for these residual-law models.

A [matched 10,000-row validation](https://ksublee.github.io/frpp/articles/legacy-fit-validation.html)
records the estimates, restoration, curvature diagnostics and elapsed times
under explicitly matched optimizer controls.

The 10,000-row maximum-likelihood fit and its reconstruction are opt-in. Set
`FRPP_RUN_LONG_EXAMPLES=true` before building this vignette to run them;
they require the optional maxLik package. The simulation, likelihood and
residual plots run in the normal build.

## One-dimensional model

The following example defines a point process with a custom residual distribution.
For details, see [Self and mutually exciting point process embedding flexible residuals and intensity with discretely Markovian dynamics](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11009-025-10159-5).
The residual density has a trapezoidal section and an exponential tail.
The `dresidual`, `presidual`, and `qresidual` functions receive their distribution parameters through the `param` vector.
The ordinary Hawkes model is the special case with an exponential residual distribution of rate 1.
Use `set_residual` to wrap the distribution functions with log-density and tail-probability support.

```{r}
mu1_d <- 0.5; alpha1_d <- 1; beta1_d <- 1.2; a <- 0.7; ell <- 1.6
hspec1_d <- set_residual(
  new("hspec", mu = mu1_d, alpha = alpha1_d, beta = beta1_d),
  param = c(a = a, ell = ell),
  dresidual = dtzexp, presidual = ptzexp,
  qresidual = qtzexp, rresidual = rtzexp
)
```

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
dh1_real <- hsim(hspec1_d, size = 3000)
hist(
  dh1_real$inter_arrival[dh1_real$inter_arrival < 3],
  breaks = 50,
  main = "Histogram of Inter-Arrival Times",
  xlab = "Inter-Arrival Time",
  ylab = "Frequency"
)
```

Use `logLik` to evaluate the observed inter-arrival times under `hspec1_d`.
Setting `infer = TRUE` also returns the intensity and residual processes in `infer_res_dh1`.

```{r, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
# Infer the residual process using the log-likelihood method
# 'infer_res_dh1' contains the inferred process data based on the inter-arrival times
infer_res_dh1 <- logLik(hspec1_d, inter_arrival = dh1_real$inter_arrival, infer = TRUE)

# Plot a histogram of the inferred residual process
hist(
  infer_res_dh1$res_process1,
  breaks = 100,
  probability = TRUE,
  main = "Histogram of Inferred Residual Process",
  xlab = "Residual Value",
  ylab = "Density"
)

x <- seq(0, 8, 0.1)

lines(
  x,
  dtzexp(x, a = a, ell = ell),
  col = 'red',
  lwd = 2
)

# Add legend for clarity
legend("topright", legend = "Theoretical PDF", col = "red", lwd = 2)

```

## Two-dimensional model

The same approach extends to multiple dimensions, using parameter matrices as in a multivariate Hawkes model.

```{r}
mu2_d <- matrix(c(0.3), nrow = 2)
alpha2_d <- matrix(c(0.5, 0.8, 0.8, 0.5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
beta2_d <- matrix(c(1.5, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
a <- 0.7; ell <- 1.6

hspec2_du <- set_residual(
  new("hspec", mu = mu2_d, alpha = alpha2_d, beta = beta2_d),
  param = c(a = a, ell = ell),
  dresidual = dtzexp, presidual = ptzexp,
  qresidual = qtzexp, rresidual = rtzexp
)
print(hspec2_du)
```


The following histogram shows inter-arrival times from a model with `tzexp` residuals.

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
set.seed(1107)
duh2_real <- hsim(hspec2_du, size = 10000)
# Plot a histogram of the inter-arrival times less than 5
hist(
  duh2_real$inter_arrival[duh2_real$inter_arrival < 5],
  breaks = 50,
  main = "Histogram of Inter-Arrival Times",
  xlab = "Inter-Arrival Time",
  ylab = "Frequency"
)
```

Use `logLik` with `infer = TRUE` to recover the intensity and residual processes.

```{r, message=FALSE}
infer_res_dh2 <- logLik(hspec2_du,
                        inter_arrival = duh2_real$inter_arrival,
                        type = duh2_real$type, infer = TRUE)
```

Under a correctly specified model, the inferred residuals follow the specified residual distribution.

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
# Plot a histogram of the inferred residual process
hist(
  infer_res_dh2$res_process2,
  breaks = 50,
  probability = TRUE,
  main = "Histogram of Inferred Residual Process",
  xlab = "Residual Value",
  ylab = "Density"
)

# Generate a sequence of x values for plotting the theoretical distribution
x <- seq(0, 8, 0.1)

# Add a line to the histogram representing the theoretical density function
lines(
  x,
  dtzexp(x, a = a, ell = ell),
  col = 'red',
  lwd = 2
)

# Add legend for clarity
legend("topright", legend = "Theoretical PDF", col = "red", lwd = 2)

```

The transformed residuals in `eres_process1` follow an exponential distribution with rate 1 under a correctly specified model.

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}
hist(
  infer_res_dh2$eres_process1,
  breaks = 50,
  probability = TRUE,
  main = "Histogram of Inferred eResidual Process",
  xlab = "Residual Value",
  ylab = "Density"
)

# Generate a sequence of x values for plotting the theoretical distribution
x <- seq(0, 8, 0.1)

# Add a line to the histogram representing the theoretical density function
lines(
  x,
  dexp(x),
  col = 'red',
  lwd = 2
)

# Add legend for clarity
legend("topright", legend = "Theoretical PDF", col = "red", lwd = 2)

```

Use `hfit` for maximum likelihood estimation.
The distribution requires `0 < a <= 3`, `ell > 0`, and a nonnegative density.
The last condition is nonlinear, so the custom objective below checks each
candidate with `dtzexp` and returns `-Inf` when the distribution is invalid.

```{r legacy-fit, warning=FALSE, eval=identical(Sys.getenv("FRPP_RUN_LONG_EXAMPLES"), "true")}
residual_loglik <- function(object, inter_arrival, type, param) {
  valid <- tryCatch({
    dtzexp(1, a = param["a"], ell = param["ell"])
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (!valid) return(-Inf)
  suppressMessages(logLik(object, inter_arrival = inter_arrival, type = type))
}
constraints <- list(
  ineqA = rbind(diag(6), c(0, 0, 0, 0, -1, 0)),
  ineqB = c(rep(0, 6), 3)
)
mle_dh <- hfit(hspec2_du,
               inter_arrival = duh2_real$inter_arrival,
               type = duh2_real$type,
               mylogLik = residual_loglik,
               constraints = constraints)
summary(mle_dh)
```

Hawkes curvature stabilization does not change this custom FRPP objective.
The moving transition point of `tzexp` can make numerical Hessians step dependent.
A successful optimizer return code does not validate the reported Wald standard
errors. See the [fit diagnostic report](https://github.com/ksublee/emhawkes/blob/main/tools/fit-diagnostics.md)
for the one-sided derivative and profile checks.

These constraints keep the six parameters nonnegative and enforce `a <= 3`, the upper limit of the trapezoid-exponential distribution.
The parameter order is `mu1`, `alpha1.1`, `alpha1.2`, `beta1.1`, `a`, and `ell`.

Reconstruction also updates the residual density, distribution, quantile, and
generator functions with the shared estimates of `a` and `ell`.
The custom objective and optimization constraints remain part of the fitting
step; `logLik()` evaluates the restored model's residual-distribution likelihood.

```{r fitted-residual-distribution, message=FALSE, eval=identical(Sys.getenv("FRPP_RUN_LONG_EXAMPLES"), "true")}
estimated_dh <- fitted_hspec(mle_dh)
initial_dh <- fit_initial_state(mle_dh)
formals(estimated_dh@rresidual)$param
inferred_dh <- do.call(logLik, c(list(object = estimated_dh,
  inter_arrival = duh2_real$inter_arrival, type = duh2_real$type, infer = TRUE), initial_dh))
c(fitted = as.numeric(logLik(mle_dh)), restored = inferred_dh$loglikelihood)
```

## Uniform residuals

The following example uses a uniform residual distribution on $[0, 2]$.

```{r, message = FALSE}

#set.seed(117)
mu2_d <- matrix(c(0.5), nrow = 2)
alpha2_d <- matrix(c(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
beta2_d <- matrix(c(1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.2), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

hspec2_du <- new("hspec", mu=mu2_d, alpha=alpha2_d, beta=beta2_d,
                 rresidual = function(size) runif(n=size, 0, 2),
                 dresidual = function(x, param = numeric(0), log = FALSE)
                   dunif(x, 0, 2, log = log),
                 presidual = function(q, param = numeric(0), lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)
                   punif(q, 0, 2, lower.tail = lower.tail, log.p = log.p),
                 qresidual = function(p, param = numeric(0), lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)
                   qunif(p, 0, 2, lower.tail = lower.tail, log.p = log.p))

duh2_real <- hsim(hspec2_du, size = 5000)
```

Plot a histogram of the inferred residuals:

```{r, message = FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}

infer_res_duh2 <- logLik(hspec2_du,
                         inter_arrival = duh2_real$inter_arrival,
                         type = duh2_real$type, infer = TRUE)

hist(
  infer_res_duh2$res_process1,
  breaks = 50,
  probability = TRUE,
  main = "Histogram of Inferred Residual Process",
  xlab = "Residual Value",
  ylab = "Density"
)

```

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
if (!emhawkes_was_attached) detach("package:emhawkes", character.only = TRUE)
```
